avoid_supplements.name: St. John's Wort
avoid_supplements.mechanism: CYP3A4 induction may reduce cimetidine efficacy; cimetidine inhibits metabolism of St. John's Wort constituents
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; consider alternative H2-blocker if St. John's Wort needed

avoid_supplements.name: High-dose Vitamin B12 supplements (cyanocobalamin)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Cimetidine reduces vitamin B12 absorption by decreasing gastric acid and intrinsic factor
avoid_supplements.action: Monitor B12 levels; use methylcobalamin or cyanoinjections instead of oral supplements

caution_supplements.name: Calcium supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: Reduced gastric acid from cimetidine may decrease calcium absorption
caution_supplements.action: Separate dosing by 2+ hours; monitor for signs of calcium deficiency; ensure adequate intake

caution_supplements.name: Iron supplements
caution_supplements.action: Space doses 2+ hours apart; consider ferrous sulfate with vitamin C for enhanced absorption

caution_supplements.name: Magnesium supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: Reduced gastric acid may impair magnesium bioavailability
caution_supplements.action: Monitor magnesium levels; separate dosing by 2+ hours

avoid_foods.name: Caffeine-containing beverages (coffee, tea, cola)
avoid_foods.mechanism: Cimetidine inhibits CYP1A2, reducing caffeine metabolism and increasing CNS stimulation risk
avoid_foods.action: Limit caffeine intake to <200mg daily; monitor for tremor, palpitations, or insomnia

caution_foods.name: High-fiber foods
caution_foods.mechanism: May slightly reduce cimetidine absorption; timing-dependent interaction
caution_foods.action: Take cimetidine 2 hours before or after high-fiber meals for optimal absorption

caution_foods.name: Fatty or heavy meals
caution_foods.mechanism: May delay cimetidine absorption; reduced gastric motility
caution_foods.action: Take on empty stomach or with light meal for best efficacy

monitoring_notes: Cimetidine is a potent CYP450 inhibitor affecting multiple pathways; monitor for drug interactions especially with medications metabolized by CYP2D6, CYP2C19, and CYP3A4. Long-term use warrants monitoring of B12 and mineral (calcium, magnesium, iron) levels due to reduced absorption from hypochlorhydria.
